units.source_text: 夕雾被鸣蜩之声惊醒，想道：“此刻山中的雾不知多么浓重，真可怜啊！

en.t: Yugiri was startled awake by the cry of the evening cicadas and thought, "How thick the mist must be in the mountains at this moment. How pitiful!

units.source_text: 今天总该写回信去了。”

en.t: Today I really must send a reply."

units.source_text: 他觉得很对不起她们，便不知不觉地拿过砚台来磨墨，一面举目怅望，考虑这回信如何写法。

en.t: Feeling deeply sorry toward them, he unconsciously drew the inkstone toward him and began grinding ink, gazing up in melancholy while considering how to compose his reply.

units.source_text: 回头忽见云居雁所坐的茵褥里边有一处稍稍高起，

en.t: When he turned back, he suddenly noticed that one place inside the cushion where Kumoinokari had been sitting was slightly raised,

units.source_text: 试把茵褥揭开一看，原来那封信塞在这里！

en.t: and when he tried lifting the cushion to look, there was the letter, tucked away inside!

units.source_text: 他又是欢喜，又是生气，笑着展开信来阅读。

en.t: Both delighted and angry, he unfolded the letter with a smile and began to read it.

units.source_text: 读完之后，心中只是叫苦。

en.t: After finishing it, he could only groan inwardly at the trouble he was in.

units.source_text: 原来老夫人以为前夜已成事实，使她心中难过，真真对她不起。

en.t: It turned out that the old lady believed the matter had already been settled the night before, and he had caused her such distress; he truly had wronged her.

units.source_text: 昨夜等到天明，不知多么痛苦。

en.t: She must have suffered terribly, waiting through the whole night until dawn.

units.source_text: 今日又到此刻尚无回音。

en.t: And now today, even by this hour, no reply had come.

units.source_text: 他想到这里，但觉懊恨不可言喻。

en.t: Thinking this far, he felt regret beyond words.

units.source_text: 又想：“老夫人熬着病苦，勉强提笔胡乱写这封信，可见她是忧伤得难于忍受，因而如此写的。

en.t: He also thought, "The old lady, enduring the pain of illness, forced herself to take up the brush and write this letter in disorder; clearly her grief was more than she could bear, and that is why she wrote as she did.

units.source_text: 怎禁得今宵又是音信全无呢！”

en.t: How could she endure another night with no word at all!"

units.source_text: 然而现已毫无办法。

en.t: Yet by now there was nothing he could do.

units.source_text: 因此觉得云居雁太恶作剧，实甚可恨。

en.t: Because of this, he felt that Kumoinokari's prank had gone too far and was truly hateful.

units.source_text: 他想：“她任情戏耍，好端端地藏过了这封信……罢了，这种习气都是我自己养成她的。”

en.t: He thought, "She played about as she pleased and hid this perfectly important letter... Well, these habits are all ones I myself encouraged in her."

units.source_text: 左思右想，觉得自身亦甚可恨，竟想哭出来。

en.t: As he turned the matter over and over, he found himself hateful as well, until he almost wanted to cry.

units.source_text: 他想立刻出门去访，又想：“公主不见得肯放心和我见面吧；但老夫人信上如此说，教我如何是好？

en.t: He wanted to go out at once to visit her, but then thought, "The princess is hardly likely to feel at ease meeting me; yet with the old lady writing this in her letter, what am I to do?

units.source_text: 真不凑巧，今天是诸事不宜的坎日，万一她们许我成亲，将来后果不吉，也使不得。

en.t: How unlucky that today is an inauspicious day for all undertakings. If they should allow me to marry her, and the result later proved ill-omened, that would not do either.

units.source_text: 还得从长计议为是。”

en.t: It would be better to consider the matter carefully over time."

units.source_text: 此人一向认真，故有此种想法。

en.t: He had always been a serious man, and so he thought in this way.

units.source_text: 于是决定先写了回信再说。

en.t: So he decided that, for the moment, he would first write a reply.

units.source_text: 信中写道：“宠锡华翰，铭感无似。

en.t: In the letter he wrote, "I am deeply grateful beyond compare for the gracious letter you have bestowed on me.

units.source_text: 拜读之余，喜不自胜。

en.t: After reverently reading it, I was overcome with joy.

units.source_text: 但‘匆匆一夜’之责，不知有何所闻而出此言？

en.t: But as for your reproach about a 'hurried single night,' I do not know what you may have heard to make you say such a thing.
